title: Push firms' costs up

predict.q: AD is fixed. Start: price level **100**, real output **1000**. Firms' input costs rise by 15 per unit of output (the input-cost index goes from 100 to 115). What happens?

options.s: SRAS shifts left: the price level rises and real output falls
options.fb: SRAS1 → SRAS2 along the fixed AD: price level 100 → 110, real output 1000 → 900.

options.s: A movement up along SRAS: the price level and real output both rise
options.fb: A movement along SRAS needs a change in the price level first. A cost change moves the whole curve; output falls, not rises.

options.s: AD shifts left: the price level and real output both fall
options.fb: Nothing in spending changed, so AD stays put. The price level rises, not falls.

options.s: SRAS shifts right: firms produce more to cover their costs
options.fb: Higher costs make each unit less profitable, so firms supply less at each price level: SRAS shifts left.

task: Move the input-cost slider and watch SRAS, the price level and real output. Then add an indirect tax.

target.do: Move the input-cost slider from 100 to 115, then press Check.

takeaway: Higher costs shift SRAS left; with AD unchanged the price level rises and real output falls (100 → 110; 1000 → 900).
